_README: Starting vocabulary for TopicClassifier (scripts/registry.py). Treat it as an EXAMPLE to replace, not as a standard: the ten subjects below are a deliberately generic set of general-interest categories, chosen to demonstrate the file format and the matching rules rather than to fit any particular research. The labels worth having are the ones your own sources fall into. Format: a top-level object of "<topic label>": ["keyword", ...]; a value must be a list of strings, never a bare string; keys beginning with '_' are documentation and are skipped. How a keyword matches is in _MATCHING, and what is deleted from the text before matching is in _STRIPPED. A source matching no keyword is left undecided, never forced into a bucket, and a source may carry several labels. A label classifies a SOURCE -- what it is mostly about -- and is not a claim about any single message in it, nor a promise that anything downstream will be built for that label. To use your own vocabulary instead of this file, see _OVERRIDING.
_MATCHING: A keyword must START a word; it is never a bare substring. Cyrillic: the tail may only be a Russian inflectional ending from the closed set in registry.py, so «банк» catches банка/банки and never «банкомат». That set has no «ия», so a stem must stop before the final vowel: «инвестици» catches инвестиция, «технолог» does not catch технология -- «технологи» does. Latin: the exact word, or a plain plural (+s/+es) on a keyword of four characters or more, so «rent» never catches «rental» and «tour» never catches «tourist» -- list both forms when both are wanted. A multi-word keyword matches as a phrase and only its last word may inflect.
_STRIPPED: normalise() deletes URLs, @handles, «по вопросам рекламы ...», «for ads ...» and the whole ad/ads/advert/advertising/advertisement family from the text BEFORE matching, so those English words can never be keywords here. The Russian «реклам*» family is untouched and would still work as a keyword.
_OVERRIDING: Editing this file changes the classifier for every project that uses this installed copy, and updating the skill overwrites it. To point one project at its own vocabulary instead, put {"topics_vocabulary": "<path to your json>"} in the file named by TELEGRAM_RESEARCH_CONFIG -- absolute, or relative to that override file itself. Your file replaces this one whole -- it is not merged with it -- so it has to carry every label you want classified.
